title: Relative operadic free mapping property for terminal active slices
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Here a symmetric infinity-operad is an inner fibration $\mathcal P^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, where $\mathrm{Fin}_*$ is the category of finite pointed sets, admitting cocartesian lifts of inert maps and satisfying the Segal product decompositions of fibers and of mapping spaces. An inert map has exactly one preimage of each non-basepoint element of its target; an active map has no non-basepoint element mapping to the basepoint. A color is an object over $\langle1\rangle=\{*,1\}$. The Segal decompositions mean that an object over $\langle n\rangle$ is a tuple of $n$ colors, and that maps over any pointed map decompose as products of the operations with each of its non-basepoint outputs. An edge of an infinity-operad is inert when it is cocartesian for its projection to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ and lies over an inert pointed map; it is active when its underlying pointed map is active. A map of infinity-operads is a functor over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ preserving inert edges.

Let $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be a cocartesian fibration that is also a map of infinity-operads, and let $\mathcal P^\otimes\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal Q^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be maps of small infinity-operads. Write $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal P/\mathcal O}(\mathcal E)$ for the infinity-category of inert-preserving functors $\mathcal P^\otimes\to\mathcal E^\otimes$ over $\mathcal O^\otimes$, with coherent transformations over that base, and similarly for $\mathcal Q$. Let $A$ be such a $\mathcal P$-algebra, $F$ such a $\mathcal Q$-algebra, and $\eta:A\to u^*F$ such a transformation. For every color $d$ of $\mathcal Q$, let
$$J_d=\mathcal P^\otimes\times_{\mathcal Q^\otimes}(\mathcal Q^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/d},$$
where the subscript $\mathrm{act}$ retains all objects and only active arrows. Suppose $J_d$ has a terminal object $(p_d,\alpha_d:u(p_d)\to d)$, and the edge
$$A(p_d)\xrightarrow{\eta_{p_d}}F(u(p_d))\xrightarrow{F(\alpha_d)}F(d)$$
is $q$-cocartesian. Then, for every $G\in\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal Q/\mathcal O}(\mathcal E)$, restriction and composition with $\eta$ induce an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal Q/\mathcal O}(\mathcal E)}(F,G)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal P/\mathcal O}(\mathcal E)}(A,u^*G).$$
These are equivalences of space-valued functors, natural in $G$ and contravariantly in the coherent category of triples $(A,F,\eta)$ satisfying the terminal-active hypotheses; a morphism of triples is a pair of algebra morphisms and a coherently commuting square for $\eta$. No colimits or presentability are assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Definition 3.1.3.1 and Proposition 3.1.3.2, with the operadic-colimit setup in section 3.1.1, especially Remark 3.1.1.4 and Lemma 3.1.1.14 (terminal-active special case). Online 2017 edition inspected; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal T$ and $r:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$ be the algebra and triple categories of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-extension-boundaries], and set $H=(A,F,\eta)$. At a color $d$, its diagram $D_d$ and cocone $c_d$ have component $F(\alpha)\eta_p$. These are coherent diagrams, because source projection, $A$, $F$, and $\eta$ are coherent functors and transformations; composing their simplices gives the stated cocone. The selected terminal object $t_d=(p_d,\alpha_d)$ has $D_d(t_d)=A(p_d)$ and $c_d(t_d)=e_d=F(\alpha_d)\eta_{p_d}$. The source of an edge of $J_d$ is an edge of $\mathcal P^\otimes$ whose image under $u$ is active. Since $u$ is over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, that source edge is active too, so $D_d$ takes values in the active subcategory. The cocone $c_d$ is active because $\eta$ lies over identities in $\mathcal O^\otimes$ and each $\alpha$ is active. The slice $J_d$ is small since both indexing operads are small. The hypothesis says exactly that $e_d$ is $q$-cocartesian.

source.place: Definition 3.1.3.1, printed p. 342: the specified active cocone from an algebra transformation.

proof.text: Fix $d$ and any finite tuple $Z$ in $\mathcal E^\otimes$. The active edge $e_d\oplus1_Z$ is $q$-cocartesian by [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. For every color $W$ the mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] therefore gives a homotopy pullback square with top row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^\otimes}(F(d)\oplus Z,W)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^\otimes}(A(p_d)\oplus Z,W)$ and the analogous bottom row in $\mathcal O^\otimes$. The same is true with all four mapping spaces restricted to active arrows. Indeed the active subspace is the inverse image of the discrete set of active pointed maps. Restrict the lower-left corner to active maps, then the right corners to active maps: composition with the active edge $e_d\oplus1_Z$ sends that lower-left subspace into the active lower-right subspace. Thus this restriction is a pullback of the original square on the indicated components, with exactly the same path data. No assertion that a nonactive map has nonactive composite is needed.

source.place: Remark 2.2.4.8 and Lemma 3.1.1.14, printed pp. 212 and 324: fixed concatenation and the cocartesian universal square.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] on $D_d\oplus Z:J_d\to\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$. The value $A(p_d)\oplus Z$ is a colimit with a cocone whose terminal component is its identity. The dual mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] shows that evaluation at $t_d$ induces an equivalence from coherent cocones $D_d\oplus Z\to\Delta W$ to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}}(A(p_d)\oplus Z,W)$: precomposing with that colimit cocone is its inverse, since evaluation of that cocone is the identity. Apply the same argument to $q(D_d\oplus Z)$ in $\mathcal O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$. The active subcategories are quasicategories: an inner-horn filler in the total quasicategory has its edges over composites of active pointed maps and hence stays active. These two evaluation equivalences commute with $q$ and with restriction along the actual cocone $c_d\oplus1_Z$; its component at $t_d$ is the edge of step 2. Therefore the local testing square in [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-extension-boundaries] is identified with the homotopy pullback square of step 2. The homotopy-pullback invariance of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] justifies replacing the two right corners by these equivalent mapping spaces, retaining the evaluation and composition homotopies. This proves the local condition for $H$, for every $d,Z,W$. In particular it proves operadic, rather than merely underlying, universality. The empty context and nullary $p_d$ are included. Terminal objects are used separately to verify a condition; no coherent choice of terminal objects as $d$ varies is required.

source.place: Remark 3.1.1.4 and Lemma 3.1.1.14, printed pp. 319 and 324: terminal-index reduction for every fixed context.

proof.text: For any triple $K=(A',F',\eta')$, consider $\rho:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal T}(H,K)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(A,A')$ induced by $r$. We prove that it lifts every $\partial\Delta^s\hookrightarrow\Delta^s$, including $s=0$. In the right-pinched model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a specified mapping-space boundary for $s>0$ gives the proper faces of $\Delta^{s+1}$ containing its final vertex; adjoin its entire initial face as the constant simplex $H$. These are all faces of $\partial\Delta^{s+1}$, with final vertex $K$. The proposed simplex on the right supplies the corresponding $\mathcal A$-simplex, constant at $A$ on the initial face. For $s=0$ prescribe the two vertices $H,K$ of $\Delta^1$ directly; the proposed right simplex is the source edge. Apply [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-extension-boundaries] with $n=s+1>0$. Its initial vertex is $H$, whose local condition was proved in step 3, and its filler preserves every specified face. The filler is precisely the required pinched mapping simplex. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $\rho$ is a trivial Kan fibration and hence an equivalence of spaces. This proves existence and contractibility of coherent extensions of transformations, including their higher simplices, rather than just a bijection of homotopy classes.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3.16 and the proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed pp. 347-348: pinched mapping-space boundary argument.

proof.text:
For a general target triple $K=(A',F',\eta')$, use $S,V,R,M$ as in [lem-coef-relative-triple-mapping-space-pullback]. The endpoint corner $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A\times\mathcal A$ is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Its pullbacks defining $\mathcal T$ are therefore quasicategories, and [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber] gives a Kan fibration $M\to S\times V$. The new strict-pullback lemma gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal T}(H,K)\cong M\times_{S\times V}(S\times R),$$
where $(a,b)\mapsto(a,u^*(b))$, compatibly with $\rho$ as projection to $S$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed p. 348: comparison of the two endpoint restrictions, written here in the coherent comma model.

proof.text:
The endpoint map in step 5 is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes. Hence [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] identifies its strict pullback with the path-space homotopy pullback
$$M\times_{S\times V}^h(S\times R).$$
The comparison inserts a constant endpoint path and preserves projection to $S$ and $R$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed p. 348: comparison of the two endpoint restrictions, written here in the coherent comma model.

proof.text: Set $U=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(A,u^*F')$, $f(a)=\eta'a$, $g(v)=v\eta$, and $h(b)=u^*(b)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] there is an equivalence $M\simeq S\times_U^hV$ with specified coherent compatibility with the endpoint projection to $S\times V$. This supplies exactly the endpoint-compatible equivalence required in [lem-coef-relative-comma-coordinate-contraction]; strict commutation of the endpoint maps is not asserted.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed p. 348: comparison of the two endpoint restrictions, written here in the coherent comma model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-comma-coordinate-contraction] to the data of step 7. It identifies the space of step 6 with $S\times_U^hR$, preserving both remaining projections up to coherent homotopy. Its endpoint-path formula is precisely the coherent square $\eta'a\simeq u^*(b)\eta$. This removes both intermediate coordinates $a_0,v_0$ and their endpoint paths, while retaining the actual source projection $\rho$ as projection to $a$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed p. 348: comparison of the two endpoint restrictions, written here in the coherent comma model.

proof.text: Now take $K=K_G=(u^*G,G,1_{u^*G})$. Then $S=U=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(A,u^*G)$ and $gh(b)=u^*(b)\eta$. The map $f$ is postcomposition with the degenerate edge $1_{u^*G}$; the maps of [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] are specified only with their coherent homotopies, and the degenerate simplices of $\mathcal A$ witness $1\circ a=a$ in every degree, so we take the representative $f=1_U$ in step 7. The identity-leg clause of [lem-coef-relative-comma-coordinate-contraction] makes projection $S\times_U^hR\to R$ an equivalence with constant-path section. Under this equivalence $\rho$ is $b\mapsto u^*(b)\eta$, with its composition homotopy. Step 4 proves $\rho$ an equivalence, so two-out-of-three proves the stated comparison an equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed p. 348: comparison of the two endpoint restrictions, written here in the coherent comma model.

proof.text: The comparison itself is the coherent transformation of space-valued functors $(H,G)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(F,G)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(A,u^*G)$ given by $b\mapsto u^*(b)\eta$. A morphism $H\to H'$ is a pair $(a:A\to A',f:F\to F')$ with the coherent square $u^*(f)\eta\simeq\eta'a$. For $b:F'\to G$, this square supplies $u^*(bf)\eta\simeq u^*(b)\eta'a$, exactly the naturality square in the contravariant triple variable. Postcomposition in $G$ gives the other variable. Their higher compatibilities are the simplices of the arrow functor category, so this constructs naturality without choosing inverses for each terminal slice. After a common universe enlargement, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says a coherent transformation is an equivalence if all its components are. Step 9 proves those components are equivalences on the full subcategory of triples satisfying the stated hypotheses. It is therefore the asserted natural equivalence of space-valued functors, with both parameter variables and all their higher simplices.
